title: Computer Systems: A Programmer’s Perspective
description: Follow a C program from source to instructions and then through the memory hierarchy. The exercises make the cost of a cache miss or an unexpected integer conversion tangible.

cover.usage: Publisher-supplied jacket in an illustrated editorial reading note.

title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
description: Virtualization, concurrency and persistence organize the book. Trace a scheduler or a lock on paper before turning to the exercises; that is where a plausible answer often reveals a race.

cover.usage: Embedded at Open Library under its public Covers API guidelines.

title: Computer Networking: A Top-Down Approach
description: Start with an HTTP request and work down the stack to the links that carry it. The authors’ packet-trace labs pair well with the chapters on transport and congestion.

cover.usage: Publisher-supplied jacket in an illustrated editorial reading note.
cover.alt: Ninth Edition badge, red title and lower band, multilevel aqueduct reflected in blue water, Kurose and Ross.
cover.difference: Matches the reference jacket. Print edition published in 2025, © 2026.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
subtitle: The Big Ideas Behind Reliable, Scalable, and Maintainable Systems
description: Use the same failure scenario to compare replication, sharding and transactions. The book explains what each design promises when a node fails, which makes it a useful companion to an architecture review.

cover.usage: Publisher-supplied jacket in an illustrated editorial reading note.
cover.alt: White cover, wild boar, orange subtitle, new Second Edition sash, two names at lower right.
cover.difference: Matches the reference. 9781098119058 is the platform identifier; the paperback’s ISBN is 9781098119065.

title: System Design Interview: An Insider’s Guide
description: Try sketching the rate limiter or chat service before reading Xu’s design. A timed comparison makes it easier to spot an assumption about capacity, latency or consistency that you left unstated.
editionNote: Volume 1 · 2020 paperback jacket marked “Second Edition”. The reference jacket is marked “Volume 1”.

title: Building Microservices
subtitle: Designing Fine-Grained Systems
description: Read the chapters on service boundaries alongside those on deployment and ownership. A split that looks tidy on a diagram can still require two teams to release at the same time.

cover.usage: Publisher-supplied jacket in an illustrated editorial reading note.

cover.difference: Matches the reference. The publisher’s online edition identifier differs from the paperback ISBN.

title: Docker Deep Dive
subtitle: Zero to Docker in a Single Book
description: Poulton follows the path from building an image to running an application with Compose. The connection between containers, networks and volumes makes this edition especially helpful for understanding what a running service needs. Its command examples reflect the 2020 toolchain.
editionNote: May 2020 paperback jacket. The reference displays the pink-banded digital design.

title: Kubernetes: Up and Running
subtitle: Dive into the Future of Infrastructure
description: The progression from a single pod to deployments and services shows which Kubernetes object is responsible when an application fails. The examples are a good fit for a first cluster. Teams managing several clusters will get more from the later chapters on organizing and shipping applications.

title: Terraform: Up & Running
subtitle: Writing Infrastructure as Code
description: Brikman connects a first deployment to the decisions that matter once a second person touches the code. The sections on shared state, reusable modules and tests are particularly useful for a team preparing to review and ship infrastructure changes together.

title: Site Reliability Engineering
subtitle: How Google Runs Production Systems
description: The chapters on service-level objectives, toil and incident response give teams a concrete way to decide when reliability deserves engineering time. The Google-scale examples work best when read alongside a service the reader actually operates.

title: Deep Learning
description: The authors start with the mathematics of learning, work through the design and training of neural networks, and then examine research problems in representation learning and generative models.

title: Designing Machine Learning Systems
subtitle: An Iterative Process for Production-Ready Applications
description: Read the deployment and monitoring chapters together when a model scores well offline but fails in service. Huyen’s account of training–serving skew gives the team a specific place to investigate. Compare how a feature is computed at training time with how it is computed for a live prediction.

title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch)
description: A reader builds a GPT-style language model in Python and PyTorch, implementing tokenization and attention before pretraining and fine-tuning the model for specific tasks.

title: AI Engineering
subtitle: Building Applications with Foundation Models
description: The evaluation and retrieval chapters work well as a pair. Tracing a poor answer back to the material retrieved for it helps a team decide whether to improve its index, change the prompt or test a different model.
